The other block, which does not get built upon, will be considered an orphaned block. Nodes that were following the orphaned block will eventually switch to the longest chain, and the transactions in the orphaned block will be returned to the pool of unconfirmed transactions, waiting to be included in a future block
This phenomenon is a natural part of how decentralized networks operate and is addressed by the consensus rules that dictate that the longest chain is the valid one
